## Research question

How are GRE score, GPA, and undergraduate institution rank associated with
graduate school admission? Admission is coded as 1 for admitted and 0 for
not admitted, so I will use logistic regression.

## Load and clean the data

```{r load-data}
raw <- read.csv("../../Data/GradSchool_Admissions.csv")
admissions <- raw[complete.cases(raw), ]
admissions$rank <- factor(admissions$rank)

nrow(raw)
nrow(admissions)
summary(admissions)
```

## Explore the data

```{r admission-by-rank}
admission_rate <- with(admissions, tapply(admit, rank, mean))
round(100 * admission_rate, 1)

barplot(
  100 * admission_rate,
  main = "Admission rate by institution rank",
  xlab = "Undergraduate institution rank (1 = top tier)",
  ylab = "Applicants admitted (%)",
  ylim = c(0, 100),
  col = "steelblue"
)
```

The observed admission rate was highest for rank 1 (54.1%) and
lowest for rank 4 (17.9%). These rates are calculated before
accounting for GRE scores and GPA.

```{r scores-by-admission, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
outcome <- factor(admissions$admit, levels = c(0, 1),
                  labels = c("Not admitted", "Admitted"))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
boxplot(gre ~ outcome, data = admissions,
        main = "GRE by admission outcome", ylab = "GRE score",
        col = "lightblue")
boxplot(gpa ~ outcome, data = admissions,
        main = "GPA by admission outcome", ylab = "GPA",
        col = "lightblue")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Admitted applicants had higher median GRE scores and GPAs, although
the distributions overlapped in both plots.

## Logistic regression

I compare a model with GRE and GPA to a model that also includes
institution rank. This tests whether rank adds information about
admission after accounting for GRE and GPA.

```{r compare-models}
model_scores <- glm(admit ~ gre + gpa,
                    data = admissions, family = binomial())

model_full <- glm(admit ~ gre + gpa + rank,
                  data = admissions, family = binomial())

AIC(model_scores, model_full)
anova(model_scores, model_full, test = "Chisq")
summary(model_full)
```

## Conclusion

I selected the model with GRE score, GPA, and institution rank because
it had a lower AIC than the model with GRE and GPA alone (470.52 vs.
486.34). The likelihood-ratio test also showed that adding institution
rank improved model fit (p = 0.000071).

In the full model, higher GRE scores and GPAs were associated with
higher odds of admission. At the same GRE score and GPA, applicants
from rank 4 institutions had about 79% lower estimated odds of
admission than applicants from rank 1 institutions. These results
describe associations in this sample.
